newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end up on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end up on weather, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Friday in a moderate session, lifted by reports of relatively firm bidweek prices and supportive weather forecasts, industry sources said.

January, which set a new high of $3.68 per million British thermal units on ACCESS, ended 13.3 cents higher at $3.437. February settled up 8.3 cents at $2.97. Others also ended up. "Forecasts are calling for well-below normal for a long time, but you could see it meltdown once the weather really gets here," said one East Coast trader.

While the market was overbought and due for a pullback, traders said storage concerns and cold weather should limit any retreat, as operators conserve stocks early in the season and buy spot to avoid a repeat of last year when sustained cold drained inventories to record lows and spiked prices.
Chartists still pegged Jan support in the mid-$3.20s and then at $3.04. Resistance was seen at the $3.68 contract high.

Cash sources said December Gulf Coast gas was talked in the low-$3.80s, with November on the same pipes was quoted in the $3.60s, down slightly on the day. December Midwest gas notionally was quoted higher near the $3.70 mark, with November softening slightly into the $3.60s. December New York city gate gas traded in the $5.05-15.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 7.1 cents to $2.401. NYMEX said 40,883 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's tally of 97,304.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 15 cents lower at $1.80, while deferred contracts were untraded but settled down 10 cents. NYMEX said 30 Alberta contracts traded versus 12 on Thursday.

NYMEX December Permian natgas settled one cent higher at $3.46 after trading early at a new benchmark of $3.50. Deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said five Permian lots changed hands compared to 12 on Thursday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian December natgas contracts expire Monday, November 25.

On the KCBT, December expired 6.2 cents higher at $3.712, while forward months ended up by two to 13 cents. The January East/West spread widened by 0.3 cents to 23.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 714 contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 905.
